sentences.text: Canadian prosecutors are seeking a 25-year prison sentence for a man who sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums in 40 countries.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: Kenneth Law pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario, Canada, though he has admitted to causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: The 61-year-old will not face charges in the UK or over any British deaths under a plea deal which saw Canadian authorities withdraw more serious charges of murder.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: During Friday's sentencing hearing in an Ontario court, prosecutors stressed that many of his victims were young and struggling with mental distress.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: If Law receives the prosecution's recommended sentence, he would serve just under 20 years in prison, after accounting for credit for time served since his May 2023 arrest.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: As she sought to make her case in court on Friday, Crown Attorney Kathleen Doherty described Law as a predator taking advantage of "vulnerable people".
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: "What they needed was help.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: But what they found was Mr Law and his products for death," Doherty said.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: She also said Law's motives were financial.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: "If people could pay, he sold it to them.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: There's no discussion or inquiries or anything going on whereby Mr Law would have any ability to appreciate the circumstances of the individual he was dealing with," she said.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: Law's defence lawyer, Matthew Gourlay, countered those claims, arguing that his client was not responsible for many of their battles with mental illness.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: He said Law held a "misguided belief" he was helping his victims.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: "Each of these incidents is its own unique tragedy," Gourlay said.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: "Mr Law may be a common denominator between them, but Mr Law was not the cause of the struggles and hardships that caused all these victims to seek out his products in the first place." Law's defence attorney has asked the court to give him a 12-year sentence.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: The sentencing hearing on Friday followed an emotional few days of testimony in September, when grieving family members and friends told the court of the pain Law had caused.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: Those impact statements will be taken into account at sentencing, which is due at a later date.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: Authorities said the former chef sold about 1,200 packages of toxic substances to recipients - who he met in online suicide forums - in 40 countries, roughly a quarter of which were sent to the UK.
sentences.article_title: Prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for 'poison seller' Kenneth Law

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'Life is not infinite': Catherine talks about mortality in new documentary clip The Princess of Wales's personal account of her experience of cancer has a soul-bearing, emotionally candid tone never presented before in a royal documentary.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: Discussing it at a private screening, she said it reflected the "fear, anxiety, uncertainty" shared by hundreds of thousands of people each year "who receive the words no one wants to hear" about having cancer.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: The documentary, Heal, being shown on BBC One on Sunday, couldn't be further away from a stiff upper lip.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: This is royal television without any palaces or carriages, it's an intense 30 minutes examining how "cancer strips everything away" and then a different kind of self-awareness emerges.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: It reveals more of Catherine's inner thoughts than any of her previous speeches and we hear more from her children than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: It changes your body, it changes you physically.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: You have to go through treatment and surgeries and everything.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: "But there's a much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: I think when you've had to confront your own vulnerabilities, you know, when you're faced with your own mortality, you have to accept that life is not infinite and in those moments, yes, a shift does happen," she says.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: Some viewers might be left in tears, others may think it's too schmaltzy - either way, they're going to be talking about it.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: It packs an emotional punch, even though it's more of a self-scripted, video diary than a conventional, journalistic documentary.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: "This will be a documentary that most people can relate to and will admire her for doing.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: There is an emotional directness that's an unusual departure," says royal commentator Prof Pauline MacLaran, of Royal Holloway, University of London.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: MacLaran thinks it will connect well with the public, who will admire Catherine's "bravery".
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: The documentary follows Catherine's Three Peaks Challenge, in which she climbed the biggest mountains in England, Wales and Scotland in a single day, and the cameras record her driving in between and her encounters with other climbers.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: This climb is a big mountainous metaphor for the difficulties, resilience and help of other people during the "scary, disorientating experience" of her treatment.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: They also all hug and kiss later, along with Prince William, with tears being brushed away.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: Those moments could be the emotional peaks that people will share, in a documentary made for the social media age.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: It's also probably the most we've heard directly from the royal children.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: Somewhere, the late Prince Philip will be scratching his head at how much the royals have dropped their tradition of privacy.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: Although we don't learn from the film the type of cancer or any details of Catherine's treatment.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: "No previous generation of the Royal Family would have considered producing something like this," says Valentine Low, author and royal commentator.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: "They would have been less willing to talk about illness and personal matters," he says.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: But this documentary is in keeping, says Low, with a generation "that's more likely to think in terms of whether there could be a positive message from the experience".
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: Nonetheless, says Low, such a film-making approach, sharing their own chosen thoughts with the camera without an interviewer, still allows Catherine to "control the narrative".
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: And there are questions that arise.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: She speaks of her cancer journey being a "pilgrimage" and the need to "spend time on our spiritual health" - and it makes you wonder whether there has been a deeply religious or spiritual experience as part of her recovery.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: There's a melancholy tone to the documentary, describing the impact of a "really dark time", and you wonder how this will sit alongside the expectations of her future royal life, when she will be queen.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: It could also raise wider questions about the treatment, waiting times and recovery support available to the great majority of NHS patients, who do not have royal titles, but whose needs are as intense.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: But we see Catherine in this documentary in hospital wards sharing experiences with other cancer patients and hearing about their hopes and fears.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: It's deliberately raw and unadorned in how it's presented.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: 'Navigating cancer is a lonely road': Catherine joins cancer support group in new documentary There are lighter moments too, joking with her brother James as they head up the mountains.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: Speaking at a screening, Catherine said the documentary was about "giving back" to people facing similar health worries and also to recognise the support of health services and charities working with patients and families.
sentences.article_title: Catherine's emotional cancer documentary strips away the stiff upper lip

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'I owe him my life' - student meets man who saved her from Huntingdon train attacker A student who survived the Huntingdon train attack has met for the first time with the passenger she believes saved her life during the stabbings.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Astrid told BBC News that Stephen Crean's decision to confront Anthony Williams gave her time to escape.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: "I owe him my life," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Williams was found guilty on Thursday of attempting to murder Crean and 13 others .
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: The then 19-year-old and 61-year-old Crean were just strangers on a train when she ran down the carriage screaming that there was a man with a knife.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Passengers on the Doncaster to King's Cross service fought off Williams, 33, with a frying pan and a toaster as the attack unfolded on 1 November 2025.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Crean ran towards Williams and was stabbed in the hands, back and neck.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: She was the last person to reach the buffet car and believes his actions gave her time to get in and shut the door.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Violent knifeman told doctor his psychosis drugs weren't working days before train attack How the Huntingdon train attack unfolded - carriage by carriage Meeting after the guilty verdicts were delivered, the two train passengers hugged.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Astrid told the Nottingham Forest fan, who had been travelling home from a match: "It's brilliant to meet you... now we will know each other for a long time." Crean said: "It means the world to me to meet her.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Meeting her was the best thing, it was worth waiting for.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: I'm just so happy." Astrid, who did not want to use her last name, said Crean was a hero for his actions that day.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: "I just owe him everything," she said, before adding: "I wouldn't be here today without you, and to put your life on the line for someone else, a complete stranger, is just complete bravery." She said Crean had a "split second to make a decision" and she owed him her life because of that.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: "So I'd just like to say thank you," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Crean praised her for alerting him to the danger of Williams as she ran past.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: "You can be proud of yourself, and your parents will be proud of you," he added.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: During the trial, Crean told the court he decided "to try to stop" the attack and "launched himself towards and at" Williams.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Crean and Astrid both faced terrifying moments as Williams rampaged down the train.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Crean said Williams asked, "Do you want to die?" as he stabbed him several times.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Crean then managed to lock himself in a toilet and call 999 telling them what had happened and that he was covered in blood and scared.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: He said he remembered seeing Astrid crying with makeup running down her face.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: The fashion student said she remembered seeing Crean throw himself at the attacker and put himself between her and Williams so she could escape.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: "I was able to shut the door with the rest of the people behind me.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: If you hadn't been in between us...
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: I have no idea what would have happened if you weren't there, literally in that second." Astrid had seen an interview with the 62-year-old on the BBC two days after the attack and contacted the BBC to say he was the man on the train who had helped protect her and others.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Only now the trial has finished have they been able to meet.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Crean said he is pleased the jury found Williams guilty of attempting to murder him as he did not believe he should be allowed to get away with the vicious attacks on him and the other passengers.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: On Thursday Cambridgeshire police apologised for failings in stopping Williams after another assault the month before the Huntingdon attack.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: As well as the train attacks, Williams was found guilty of attempting to murder four other people in separate incidents and will be sentenced at Cambridge Crown Court on 4 and 5 February.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: Crean believes more should have been done to prevent these further offences.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: "I think they should have had him before.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: He shouldn't have been allowed to go running around like this.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: And if they'd picked up on it, we'd have had him before." Having survived the attack, Astrid is running the London marathon for Crimestoppers as part of her efforts to turn around the harrowing situation she found herself in.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: She can, she says, because of Stephen Crean's actions.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.text: And he has promised to be there for her again: this time on the finish line.
sentences.article_title: 'I wouldn't be here today without you': Student's praise for man who stopped Huntingdon train attacker

sentences.article_title: Why snooker could be the most mentally challenging sport

sentences.article_title: Why snooker could be the most mentally challenging sport

sentences.text: Photonic chips use light instead of electrons to process data "Photonic chips are on the verge of a breakthrough," says Ton van Mol of the Dutch research institute TNO.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If van Mol is right – and TNO, the European Union and the Dutch government are backing the idea with millions of euros - then the technology could be a gamechanger.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The chips which run today's society, from your phone and TV, to the vast data centres meeting our insatiable desire for AI, are mostly electrical.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: They process data by shunting electrons around tiny circuits – a single microchip produced today can contain billions of transistors, and sizes are measured in nanometres (one nanometre is a billionth of a metre).
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Van Mol hopes for an acceleration in photonics similar to the one seen in electrical chips since the 1970s.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "With optical chips, you are now where electronic chips were maybe 40 [or] 50 years ago." American, Taiwanese and Chinese firms dominate the computer chip industry, but Europe sees the emergence of photonic chips as a fresh opportunity to lead, on what could be, a key future technology.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why the European Union has committed €400m ($450m; £330m) to a project called PIX Europe , external , with the stated goal of making the continent "a global leader in emerging technology for Photonic Integrated Chips".
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe said 'we need to have our own manufacturing in-house'," says van Mol, who is leading a key part of the programme.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Factories with machines that can handle bigger wafers can churn out chips more efficiently.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "[Photonic chip] manufacturing worldwide is [currently] done on wafers which are four inches (10cm) in size, and the next step is to scale-up production to a six-inch wafer," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: His team are already building a 10,000 sq m factory to produce six-inch indium phosphide wafers on the High Tech Campus in the Dutch city of Eindhoven.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's due to fully open in 2030 and will be a major step forward, not just for photonics in Europe, but around the world, according to van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "That's the development TNO is going to do, in a pilot line which is really serious.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The Netherlands-based tech giant is the only company in the world able to build the machines needed to make the most sophisticated semiconductors.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why ASML products will sit at the heart of the pilot line in Eindhoven - it's no coincidence that van Mol's project is based around the corner from ASML's headquarters.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "The way you produce these [photonic] chips is very similar to the way you produce electrical or electronic chip," says van Mol.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "You use the same type of equipment, you also need a high-end clean room, you also use wafers, so the production method is very similar to the traditional semiconductor technology." ASML itself is keen to explore the opportunities that the emerging technology of photonics could offer.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe has a strong position in photonics research.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The next challenge is translating those innovations into industrial-scale manufacturing," says Stanislas Baron, who is the head of ASML's EU/US Customer Team.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The Eindhoven project has the backing of former ASML chief executive Peter Wennink, author of an influential report for the Dutch government called The Roadmap to Future Prosperity , external , which noted that the market for photonics was expected to grow 10 to 20 times in the next 10 years.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: In a news release backing the new pilot line, Wennink described it as "a launchpad for Europe's future digital economy".
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "By investing in scalable production capacity, we are creating an ecosystem that can help shape the global technological direction," he said.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Of course, Europe is not alone in looking to the potential of photonics to earn a global economic advantage.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: In June this year, US photonics company Coherent announced what it called "the world's first and largest volume-production six-inch indium phosphide manufacturing platform" at its plant in Sherman, in Texas.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The expansion is backed by chip manufacturing giant Nvidia , external , as well as $50 million public funds under the US Chips Act.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's an illustration of how quickly the market is moving, and how central photonic chips could be to the continuing race to retain an influential stake in AI and technological development more generally.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Europe's bid to establish itself as a global leader in photonic chips – exemplified by the Eindhoven project – is the kind of strategy that makes sense in a globalised economy, says Joris Teer, policy analyst at the European Institute for Security Studies in Brussels.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If the continent can take a lead in photonic chips, then future developments in AI and data will partly be dependent on Europe.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "Europe knows that its high energy and labour costs, skilled workforce shortages, and lack of private and public capital make an across-the-board reindustrialisation strategy impossible", Teer says.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "To retain influence, ensuring dependence on European parties rather than European autonomy is key." Once up and running, the Eindhoven project will provide a pilot production line which can be used multiple companies.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It will be open to businesses across Europe and beyond, who can design and build chips without having to develop their own expensive production facilities.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Instead, they will produce to order for outside customers.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: It's the same idea which, at huge scale, has brought Taiwanese-based giant TSMC a position of global dominance in the manufacture of microchips.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Photonic chips are already in use, in highly specialised areas in data centres and in Lidar (light detection and ranging) sensor technology, for instance.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Lord Mandelson still held shares in his lobbying company eight months after becoming US ambassador, despite government concens about conflicts of interest, newly released documents show.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: The peer was sacked as ambassador last year by Sir Keir Starmer following revelations about the extent of his relationship with the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: This 85-page release is the third since MPs voted to publish documents aiming to reveal behind-the scenes-discussions about how he was appointed to the role.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: The documents were previously withheld due to the Metropolitan Police investigation into allegations Lord Mandelson had passed market-sensitive government information to Epstein.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: Sir Olly Robbins was sacked as head of the Foreign Office by Sir Keir Starmer during the scandal when it emerged Lord Mandelson had been granted clearance for the role despite concerns being raised by vetting officials.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: The newly released documents highlight that Lord Mandelson was able to keep his shares in Global Counsel, the lobbying company he co-founded, while serving as ambassador to Washington.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: They reveal civil servants' concerns about the risk of perceived conflict of interest.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: But selling the shares was clearly not a condition of him taking up the role.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: Part of that is because of the desire in Sir Keir's government at the time to have Lord Mandelson in Washington as quickly as possible.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: That is exemplified in an email from Sir Olly, saying a process to police Mandelson's conflicts of interest could be "up and running in a light touch way".
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: Another factor is selling shares in a private company like Global Counsel, which advised high-profile clients including Chinese-owned TikTok, US tech firm Palantir and pharmaceutical firm GSK. requires finding a new buyer or selling them back to the company.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: But the documents also reveal Lord Mandelson had not sold his shares back to Global Counsel because their offer was not the "fair value".
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: Another attempt to sell to a different buyer fell through.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: The result was Mandelson kept his shares, and while in office tried to set up a meeting between Global Counsel and a key Donald Trump advisor, as well as taking the firm's advice on a speech on Britain's role in the world.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: Lord Mandelson remained a shareholder until February 2026 , the same month the company went into administration.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: Ahead of  a speech he was due to give on Britain's role "in the age of Trump", documents show him seeking advice from a Global Counsel employee in August 2025, during his time as ambassador.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: The exchange contains feedback from an unnamed Global Counsel director, who suggested he should use "warmer language" about China and tone down "parts of your apologia of the Trump administration".
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: On the domestic front, Lord Mandelson also sent texts to Sir Keir's then chief of staff Morgan McSweeney in September 2025 offering advice on a cabinet reshuffle.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: He suggested moving Darren Jones to lead the science and technology department as a way to "solve your Darren issue", although McSweeney did not respond until after the reshuffle decisions had been made, with Jones given a newly-created role as chief secretary to the prime minister.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: Lord Mandelson has yet to comment on the most recent release of papers relating to his appointment.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: He has repeatedly let it be known he believes he has not acted criminally, did not act for personal gain and is cooperating with the police.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: No charges have been made.
sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.article_title: Mandelson kept shares as ambassador despite conflict of interest fears, documents show

sentences.text: Alan Feeney stepped down from Reform UK after the comments emerged Four council seats in the West Midlands have been defended by Reform UK after by-elections triggered by the resignation of a councillor featured in an ITV News undercover investigation , external .
sentences.article_title: Reform wins by-elections after offensive comments

sentences.text: Alan Feeney, who later stepped down from the party , was filmed calling Asian homeowners "parasites", in the run up to council elections in May.

sentences.text: Sarah Myers was voted in to replace Feeney in Shard End, edging Labour by 104 votes, with Birmingham City Council recording a voter turnout of 19%.

sentences.text: Speaking after her win, she said: "I am delighted to have been elected for Shard End, and I'm excited to get to work delivering for local residents.
sentences.article_title: Reform wins by-elections after offensive comments

sentences.text: "Shard End was a former Labour stronghold, and has been badly let down over decades of neglect.
sentences.article_title: Reform wins by-elections after offensive comments

sentences.text: "I look forward to proving that the confidence residents have in Reform is well placed." A Reform UK Birmingham spokesperson said the results showed the public were "sticking with Reform".
sentences.article_title: Reform wins by-elections after offensive comments

sentences.text: "The good people of Shard End recognise that Reform is a patriotic party of good, hard-working individuals who want to fix our country," they added.
sentences.article_title: Reform wins by-elections after offensive comments

sentences.article_title: Reform wins by-elections after offensive comments

sentences.article_title: Reform wins by-elections after offensive comments

sentences.text: Reform UK is promising to scrap parking fees at NHS hospitals in England for all patients, visitors, and staff if it wins power at the next election.

sentences.text: The party said rising parking charges in recent years were unfair, with some hospitals charging up to £20 a day for parking spots.
sentences.article_title: Reform UK pledges to scrap hospital parking fees in England

sentences.text: It says it would compensate hospital trusts for the £300m they currently get from fees each year by raising more from foreign visitors using the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Reform UK pledges to scrap hospital parking fees in England

sentences.article_title: Reform UK pledges to scrap hospital parking fees in England

sentences.text: Reservist soldiers training at Longmoor camp in southern England in 2024 (file photo) The Ministry of Defence has written to ex-military personnel to check their contact details and skills against the backdrop of a rising "threat environment", Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has said.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: It comes after The Times and the Telegraph reported that reservists who previously served in the Armed Forces have received letters telling them to prepare to be called up for war.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: Streeting told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that this meant should they ever be needed  "either for a national disaster here at home or for a more serious threat or conflict elsewhere" then they would "know where our strategic reserve is" and what their skills were.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: "I want the country to be alert, not alarmed," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: "You can't not look at what's going on in Europe and not be concerned about a threat environment which has deteriorated in recent years and is sadly increasing," Streeting told Today.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: "We saw last Friday a very serious incident – the incursion into Polish airspace by Russian missiles, we've seen state-sponsored terrorism waged by Russia across Europe, we've obviously had incidents concerning Iran around RAF bases here in the UK.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: This is not a case of pressing the panic button for imminent war, but more one of good housekeeping.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: When Britain went to war in Iraq in 2003 the MoD had a poor grasp of who might be available to serve, what current skills they had and what their up-to-date contact details were.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: So they obviously don't want to be in that situation if there is a national crisis in the future that triggers a mobilisation.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: Twenty three years on, the Ukraine war has changed everything.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: It's brought a hot war to the very borders of Nato, it's exposed the dangers of having too few troops available, but most of all it has changed the nature of warfare.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: People who have spent their adult lives never touching a weapon can turn out to be extraordinarily skilled drone operators, those with a talent for electronics, radio and signals work have a vital role to play in electronic warfare.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: So this exercise by the government, probably long overdue, is about knowing who can do what and where they can be contacted.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: Justin Crump, a former Army officer and now CEO of the business intelligence firm Sibylline, told the BBC: "Ukraine has shown us the importance of mobilising civilian skills and approaches in modern warfare.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: This is a first step, and an overdue one in many ways, with the effort likely to increase through early 2027. [It is] very much a part of deterrence and not an intention to use people".
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: He said veterans - a sometimes misleading term for men and women who are often in peak physical shape and fitness - that he has contacted have generally responded positively to the move.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: "After all", he said, "they signed up to help before, but want to make sure their enhanced skills and talents are valued".
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: The MoD's decision to contact ex-military personnel comes after news that the UK has signed an £8bn contract to upgrade its nuclear submarine fleet, which the defence secretary said would help get the country "warfighting ready".
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Streeting also praised the Duke of Sussex's "patriotic spirit" after the former Army officer said he would rejoin the armed forces again if needed.
sentences.article_title: UK reservists contacted as 'threat environment' rises, Streeting says

sentences.text: "I think that's exactly the sort of patriotic spirit we're looking for," he said.

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham and a number of previous prime ministers attended the service Andy Burnham was joined by former prime ministers as he attended a memorial service for the late politician Ann Widdecombe.

sentences.text: Finishing the eulogy, he said: "We loved her very much, and we'll miss her." sentences.text: Forty-eight people were killed when Sir Galahad was attacked in 1982 A Falklands War veteran who was left severely burned in an attack on his ship has accused ministers of hiding behind data protection in refusing to release all files on the bombing.

sentences.article_title: Ministers hiding behind data protection on Sir Galahad bombing files, says veteran

sentences.article_title: Ministers hiding behind data protection on Sir Galahad bombing files, says veteran

sentences.article_title: Ministers hiding behind data protection on Sir Galahad bombing files, says veteran

sentences.article_title: Ministers hiding behind data protection on Sir Galahad bombing files, says veteran

sentences.text: A review of the main disability benefit has recommended an overhaul of the system to allow disabled people to "achieve better health, higher living standards and greater independence".

sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The benefit is claimed by four million people and is available to people whether they are in work or unemployed.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Its aim is to help with the additional costs of being disabled.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.

sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: More than 40,000 disabled people engaged with the process with more than 90% of them saying they'd had a negative experience while applying for Pip, describing it as stressful, dehumanising or psychologically damaging.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The review concludes the Pip process is "not fit for purpose" and calls for a fundamental redesign.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: While the review was chaired by Sir Stephen Timms, the disability minister, the experience of disabled people is clear throughout the review.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: A fast-track process should be introduced for two types of claimants.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Those with terminal illnesses should get the fastest route to an award to ensure their lives are as comfortable as possible.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Those who have severe conditions that are well-evidenced and unlikely to change over time, and whose impact on daily living is clear, should also receive the benefit without a full assessment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Any subsequent review should avoid unnecessary reassessments.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Other claimants will have to go through an updated initial assessment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: This will examine how a person's condition affects their daily life – functions, barriers, and needs that are currently not being met.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: This assessment will determine entitlement to the benefit.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: It will also decide the level of cash award, which will remain the bedrock of the benefit.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Optional referrals to support services should also be offered but this will be voluntary and a refusal to engage with them should not affect the benefit level.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: A new set of questions should be developed to better understand the extra costs a person faces, but will not ask them to calculate costs or provide receipts.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The system should recognise fluctuating and cumulative needs and produce decisions that are consistent and be robust against misuse.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The 28-day hospitalisation rule – which sees Pip payments suspended if someone spends more than 28 days as an inpatient – should also be reviewed as claimants find it can cause unnecessary stress and can delay discharges from hospitals.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The inquiry was not set up to find savings in the system despite the fact that spending on Pip is forecast to cost more than £40bn by 2030.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: In the year before the Covid pandemic, Pip cost £16.3bn when adjusted for inflation to today's prices.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The review is not explicit on who these people might be.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: It will be up to the government to decide how they marry the two reports.

sentences.text: Sales of a baby sleeping bag have been halted in the UK by fashion retail chain Next, after a new mum raised the alarm over its safety.

sentences.text: Yellow arrows indicate the tumours visible before treatment Experts are calling it the biggest breakthrough in pancreatic cancer treatment for decades - a daily pill that appears to shrink and possibly even eliminate tumours in some patients with one of the deadliest and hardest-to-treat cancers.

sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "What this new drug has done is it's found a way of drugging the undruggable.

sentences.text: "We are finally seeing progress in pancreatic cancer which is so long overdue." Pancreatic cancer is notoriously hard to treat and has the lowest survival rate of all common cancers in the UK.

sentences.text: "We are beginning to see not only a higher percentage of tumour response rates, but also deeper responses and a near doubling in the duration of disease control, which may eventually translate into longer survival," he said.

sentences.text: Jenny Keane said NIAS has been offered extra resources to address the issue, but added the money would only cover extra paramedic shifts, not more ambulances.

sentences.text: Keane, who took charge of NIAS in July, made her remarks on Thursday as she briefed Stormont's health committee on the challenges the service is facing.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: At the outset, she apologised over NIAS's inability to meet emergency targets across Northern Ireland as a whole, acknowledging that some patients "have died while waiting" on an ambulance to arrive.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: NIAS chief executive Jenny Keane gave evidence to Stormont's Health Committee "Our average ambulance response time to our patients in Northern Ireland are the slowest in the United Kingdom and are consistently failing to get to patients within the standard we aim for," she said.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: "This is unacceptable and intolerable." Keane said the average response times for "category one" 999 calls so far this year has been 11 minutes, compared to a standard target of eight minutes.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: She added that NIAS's average response to category two calls was 64 minutes, where the target is 18 minutes.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: A category one call is defined as situation where a patient's life is at immediate risk.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: A category two call is still a 999 emergency - it is defined as a "potentially serious incident" but can include patients suffering a suspected stroke or cardiac chest pain.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: Keane acknowledged that delayed ambulance response times puts patients at risk.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: "This is not the level of service that we want to provide and I want to apologise to our service users and all those who have experienced or been affected by a poor ambulance response," she said.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: Health committee chair Philip McGuigan of Sinn Féin thanked Keane for her candid briefing and asked how many patients had come to harm due to the delays.
sentences.article_title: Concern over maternity unit move prompts extra paramedic funding

sentences.text: Early efforts to contain coronavirus "were doomed to fail" because the test, trace and isolate system in the UK could only handle a relatively small number of cases, the seventh report of the Covid inquiry says in a damning assessment.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Across 245 pages the inquiry looks at everything from border controls to how well contact tracing worked.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report said the virus was allowed to spread virtually unchecked in the first few months after community testing and contact tracing was abandoned in mid-March 2020, costing lives.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers said this was because testing capacity was being overwhelmed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: NHS Test and Trace was launched two months later and eventually became one of the biggest testing services in the world per head of population.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the end, more than £30bn was spent across the UK during the pandemic on testing, tracing and isolating.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Once established, it was effective.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But in those early months the four UK nations were "effectively blind" to how quickly Covid was spreading, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It criticises the government for not having a robust test, trace and isolate system in place to start with, saying this, alongside other failures, meant harsher measures, including lockdown and school closures, were needed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Inquiry chair Baroness Hallett said the UK should have been better prepared and learnt lessons from other countries that had experience of dealing with outbreaks of other infectious diseases, such as Sars.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Unlike the UK, places such as Hong Kong, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan had established systems ready to go.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: This was despite the fact the UK had run a series of simulation exercises in the years leading up to Covid.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: They included Exercise Cygnus into a flu pandemic and Exercise Alice into Mers.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Both identified problems relating to test, trace or isolation, which appear not to have been fully acted on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report also raises the question of whether the government could have made use of non-government testing facilities in hospitals, universities and the private sector from the start, instead of just relying on 12 government labs.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: When people in the UK were told to isolate, "many felt forgotten and let down by the lack of practical or financial support when trying to follow the rules", says the report.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the early months of the pandemic, estimates suggested less than half of people were complying with the rules around isolating if infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers and their advisers discussed this and fines of up to £10,000 were introduced for those who did not comply, which some experts have said was counter-productive.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Changes were made to allow people to claim statutory sick pay.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But it was not until September in England – and later in Scotland and Wales – that £500 financial payments were introduced to help those on low incomes comply.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: More also needed to be done to provide practical support for things such as collecting medicines and shopping for food for those who did not have people to call on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Suspending all flights from China to the UK in February 2020 could "have provided valuable additional time to prepare healthcare systems for the impact of the pandemic", said inquiry chair Baroness Hallett.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says the UK lacked a clear strategy for implementing border control measures early in the pandemic, which left the country in an "extremely vulnerable position".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: By contrast, the UK government only requested travellers arriving from high-risk areas to self-isolate for 14 days.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The UK government implemented no further border control measures until June 2020.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says that border controls were a "critical gap in the UK's ability to limit the spread of the virus" and recommends that in the future "international border control measures should be in place at the earliest stages of a pandemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry report is more positive about the use of smartphone apps, saying digital tools can have a "significant impact on reducing the spread of infection".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes a mathematical modelling study from the US which estimates that, when 75% of people used a contact tracing app in the pandemic, infections were reduced by at least 50%.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Three different apps were developed during Covid - one for England and Wales, another for Scotland and a third for Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry says that took up "valuable time", and it recommends developing a UK-wide digital tool to use in any future outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It says it is "fundamentally important" that apps and digital tools are as accurate as possible – and people have confidence in them.

sentences.text: Under Kennedy's leadership, a US vaccine panel attempted to end a longstanding recommendation that all newborns receive a hepatitis B vaccine at birth, but a federal judge later blocked this, along with other changes to vaccine policy made by the Trump administration.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Critics have questioned whether the research could help support that policy shift, although the study's stated aim was to investigate potential effects of the vaccine beyond preventing infection.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Kennedy has praised the Danish researchers as "the deities of vaccine research", and cited earlier findings from their work in support of concerns about vaccine safety.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: A subsequent study by some of the same researchers, however, found no evidence of the previously reported effect.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: There is no evidence that the proposed trial was designed to justify a change in US policy.

sentences.text: Schools in England have been told to prepare for emergencies including national power outages and water shortages under updated government guidance.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: New action cards, which provide practical steps for staff to take during an incident, have been issued to schools for the first time to help them respond immediately.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: Loss of connectivity, cyber attack, environmental hazards and extreme weather are all listed as possible incidents that could seriously disrupt education.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) said schools "already strive to remain open in emergency situations and only take the decision to close where there is no alternative option".
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: The union said schools and colleges have robust emergency plans and procedures in place which are regularly reviewed and updated.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: The updated guidance , external for all education and childcare settings follows lessons learned from recent events, including wildfires and cyber attacks.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: The Department for Education says the cards , external should form part of every school's existing emergency planning and staff training.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: The guidance says closing schools would not necessarily reduce the risk to children and young people, as the same emergency may also affect their homes or the wider community.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: "Remaining at the setting may sometimes be the safer option," it says.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: Head teachers are being asked to consider how long their schools could remain open if critical services were disrupted, including overnight.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: The guidance says plans should show how they would support anyone unable to be collected or who needed to remain on site overnight.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: They should also set out how they would obtain water, food and essential medical supplies if deliveries were disrupted.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: Schools should also refer to the National Risk Register, which sets out the most significant risks facing the UK, when planning for emergencies, the guidance says.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the government warned that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households needed to have enough supplies to last three days as part of its "Be Ready" campaign.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: Meet the people around the world already preparing for crisis Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch The cards cover what to do in the event of flooding, heatwaves, health incidents such as infectious disease outbreaks, utility disruptions and security-related events.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: They also include advice on dealing with suspicious drone activity, hoax threats and smoke from wildfires.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: In the event of a national power outage, for example, the advice includes filling up "potable water supplies", using fresh food first and preparing for wider community use if requested.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: If a school were to lose all connectivity, including online services and telephone lines, the guidance says it should confirm how it would contact 999 and use paper registers where necessary.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: The government says further action cards may be added in the future.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: It also says they should be accessible during disruptions to power, connectivity or digital systems.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: Universities and higher education providers are expected to apply the guidance proportionately too.
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: Tom Middlehurst, from ASCL, said incidents like this summer's "intense heatwaves" - which led to hundreds of schools either fully or partially closing - "happen very quickly and entail having to make decisions and communicate them to families and staff at pace".
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather

sentences.text: He said schools' "number one priority at all times" was the safety and wellbeing of students and staff, adding that it was "not particularly helpful" of the government to "lecture them about the importance of staying open".
sentences.article_title: Schools given emergency action plans for power outages and extreme weather
