sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: There were just under one million young people aged 16 to 24 not in employment, education or training (Neet) in the UK in the three months to September, according to new data.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: Thursday's figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) recorded 959,000 people who were Neet in that time, a very slight increase on the same period a year ago, though the number of women who were Neet was at its highest in a decade.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: The data comes a week after a major review by former government minister Alan Milburn set out a series of recommendations to bring the numbers down.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the government was "fundamentally reforming how we support young people".
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: Thursday's figures from the ONS , external suggest there were 17,000 more young people who were not earning or learning this summer compared to the same period last year.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: The overall number of 959,000 young people who were Neet this summer represents 12.7% - about one in eight - of the whole UK population aged 16 to 24.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: The rate has dropped slightly, by 0.3 percentage points, compared to earlier in the year, with 22,000 fewer young people recorded as Neet between July and September than in April to June.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: The Neets data tends to fluctuate across the year with seasonal hiring patterns and academic summer holidays.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: The changes in the latest figures are also within the margin of error of the Labour Force Survey which the stats are based on.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: In his long-awaited report into youth employment, published earlier this month , Milburn set out proposals aimed at bringing the Neet rate down to 5% over the next decade.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: If successful, that would put the UK in line with some of the lowest rates in Europe.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: Currently, only Romania has a higher Neet rate than the UK.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: Milburn called for a "whole system reset" across education, health and welfare to achieve that.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: It would include an overhaul of the benefits system for under-25s, new legal rights to work and training opportunities and plans to expand college places and double the number of young people taking up apprenticeships.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: The government has broadly accepted Milburn's proposals, but is yet to respond to all the plans in detail.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report In the data, Neets can be categorised as either unemployed - which means they are actively seeking work - or economically inactive - meaning they are not seeking work, which could be because of illness or caring responsibilities.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: Most young people who are Neet fall into the economically inactive category, with  596,000 young people economically inactive in the latest stats, compared to 363,000 who were unemployed.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: Overall, there are still more young men who are Neet (483,000) but the number of young women who are Neet is at its highest level in a decade, at 476,000.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: Ben Harrison, from the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, says the higher number of women out of work could be partly down to the loss of a "significant" number of jobs in retail, a sector in which "historically, many young women have taken their first steps into work".
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: Responding to the latest Neets figures, McFadden said "every one" of the young people out of education, employment or training "deserves better".
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: "That's why we're fundamentally reforming how we support young people to grow up in this country," he said.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: He said the government was "building a new settlement that invests in young people's success instead of paying for failure" in the wake of the Milburn review.
sentences.article_title: Number of young people out of work or training still stubbornly high, data shows

sentences.text: "That includes a Jobs Guarantee offering eligible young people on universal credit a fully funded six-month job, as well as thousands more work experience placements, and youth hubs bringing employment, health, and skills support under one roof." sentences.text: Georgia Harrison says young people are being exposed to "poison" online TV celebrity and "revenge porn" victim Georgia Harrison has urged MPs to back a new law that would extend compulsory relationships and sex education (RSE) up to the age of 18.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: The Only Way Is Essex and Love Island star led a protest outside Parliament to call for the change, telling the BBC it was needed to combat the "poison" young people were being exposed to online.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: The demonstration comes ahead of a debate and vote next week on a draft law that would legally require all further education providers in England to teach RSE to under-18s.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: The Department for Education (DfE) said it was exploring how RSE could be extended to colleges.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: Compulsory relationships and sex education currently stops at age 16 in England, meaning sixth forms and colleges are not required to teach the subject.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: Speaking in Westminster, Harrison said: "Between 16 and 18 is the age that people first start having sex.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: "It doesn't make sense that we're abandoning them at that time." Harrison said "misogynists" had "sold our young people advice, but really, it's poison".
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: "We need to undo it and the only way to undo it is through education," Harrison said.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: Harrison was a victim of so-called revenge porn .
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: Fellow reality TV performer Stephen Bear was jailed for posting intimate footage of the pair online, which he had filmed at his home in Loughton in Essex.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: She said making RSE mandatory to age 18 could help prevent intimate image abuse of the kind she suffered.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: The campaign outside Parliament was organised by media organisation LADbible.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: The Relationships and Sex Education (Further Education Sector) Bill has been put forward by Alistair Strathern, the Labour MP for the Hitchin constituency in Bedfordshire and Hertfordshire.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: It is a private members' bill, which are only debated on Fridays and rarely become law.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: However, Strathern told the BBC he had "a good chance of making real change".
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: "I've been really encouraged by the response we've got from ministers so far," he said.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: Georgia Harrison, pictured with Alistair Strathern MP, says stopping sex education at 16 "doesn't make sense" A DfE spokesperson said: "Supporting children and young people to grow up happy and healthy whilst safeguarding them from harm on and offline is a job for us all.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: "We're determined that across our education system, schools and colleges play their part.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: "That's why we have rolled out mandatory RHSE [relationships, sex and health education] in schools and we are exploring how we can extend this to colleges too." The bill follows a petition by the survivor-led campaign group Make it Mandatory, which called for sex education to be mandated to 18.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: Faustine Petron said she founded the campaign after surviving a coercive and abusive relationship when she was under 18.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: "I thought back to the lack of education I had about the signs of abusive behaviour, grooming and coercive control," Petron said.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: "I was shocked in my research to find out that sex education ends at 16.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: I thought 'how nonsensical'.
sentences.article_title: Reality TV star backs extending sex education to 18

sentences.text: "I got into the relationship at 16.

sentences.text: Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: In a major review, published on Tuesday, , external he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser.

sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.

sentences.text: Pupils will not be allowed access to their phones at all during the school day under stricter government guidance in England.

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Ministers now say changes to that guidance will go beyond the current "no see, no hear" policies in place in some schools - where phones can remain in pupils' bags if they are not seen or heard - when it comes into force from September 2027.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Access to phones "risks pulling children away from their learning and from each other", the government said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Schools will be able to decide how to follow the guidance.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Some schools have invested in sealed pouches or secure lockers.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Others collect phones at the start of the day, or have prohibited them from sites altogether.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Powell said such policies could achieve a "whole-school culture change" - and that was "what we want to see happening everywhere".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Karl Harrison, head teacher at Burnage Academy for Boys in Manchester, told the programme the school had spent £20,000 to bring in a system of metal detectors and phone pouches to prevent pupils from accessing their phones.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: While some felt their freedom had gone, locking phones away had increased how much pupils socialised at school, he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "People now can talk to each other, instead of scrolling on a device," he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "If all schools are going to be expected to have lockable pouches or other secure storage facilities for every pupil, the cost involved will be very significant indeed," he said.

sentences.text: "This is not feasible unless the government puts in the funding required to meet these costs." Responding to questions about funding, Powell told BBC Breakfast that she wanted heads to have the autonomy to implement the policies that work best for their schools.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: The government has warned some schools start teaching GCSEs in the first year of secondary school Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught in England.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "I'm putting a stop to that." A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.

sentences.text: I've just spent a week using Muse, Meta's AI agent that rolls out in the UK today.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Agents are systems that don't just respond to questions but can carry out tasks for you.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: With Muse, Meta gives the examples of "searching for a cheaper energy deal" or "sorting the school calendar." And it's true that it has helped me run my life - but it also challenged my personal privacy boundaries, and made me endure some cringeworthy interactions.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: How well Muse works really matters to Meta.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It has made a truly enormous bet on AI - of the $145bn (£111bn) it will spend this year much of it will be on building out the tech.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: For that to pay off we all need to start using it much more, and Meta hopes Muse will do for AI agents what WhatsApp did for messaging - that is, become the AI agent of choice for billions of people, putting Meta at the forefront of the AI revolution.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: But it's not just about what consumers think.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Regulators are keeping a careful eye on these emerging tools too.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "Agentic AI has significant potential to benefit people and businesses", the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) noted as Muse launched in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: But its chief executive, Paul Arnold, added it had been "clear with Meta about its responsibilities under data protection law prior to launch, particularly the requirement to ensure that users and the wider public can meaningfully understand and control how their personal data is used in the Muse product".
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Muse bills itself as a personal AI agent available to anyone aged 18 and over.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "It doesn't just answer questions, it actually goes out and does work for you," said David Singleton, Meta's VP of engineering on AI products.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "So it helps people stay on top of things," he added.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It won't book the holiday without your permission - but it can then make the purchase, if you let it.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: And the permission requests keep on coming.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Every time Muse wants to do something, send something or post something, you have to allow it.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It is reassuring to know that an AI agent isn't running amok in your name, even if it also gets a bit annoying, though you can give it more autonomy (and so get fewer messages) if you adjust the settings.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Muse can't access many apps at the moment but the fundamental ones are the most personal.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I found myself wincing as I hooked it up to one of my personal email accounts, my personal calendar and my personal phone messages.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I did not allow it any access to my BBC accounts.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It can't access WhatsApp except to set up a separate chat between it and the user, and while it found me some train tickets, it could not book them via the app which I use, and which is cheaper.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It ended up telling me to book them myself.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Amazon has blocked it from its marketplace, citing data security concerns but my agent didn't seem to know that, and spent a fruitless hour repeatedly telling me it was still waiting for the page to load in order to find me some shelves.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: A number of big UK firms are working with Meta though, including Marks & Spencer, Debenhams Group, Currys, Sainsbury's and Ocado.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: The ICO is urging consumers to be cautious with AI agents though: "consider the pros and cons," it said in a blog post to coincide with Muse's launch. , external "Agents can make mistakes.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Mistakes can be magnified if the agent is acting autonomously," it noted.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Meta is keen to emphasise how its agents can be personalised: "No two Muses are alike," , external it says in its press release.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I called my agent Linda - after the robot in the BBC TV series Ann Droid - but it can take any form you like.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I gave it a British, female accent from the myriad of choices available.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: As soon as an email came in, it would summarise it for me and suggest a reply.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Sometimes a long time before I was actually ready to respond.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Sometimes, if I hadn't interacted with it for a while, generally because I was busy, it would pop up with some random prompt like "did you know you can change my outfit?" I expect this is designed to drive engagement: Muse is only free to use until a certain point, and then subscriptions kick in.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It also wrote some embarrassing replies to messages on my behalf: in response to a question about whether I would like to go on an outing, for example, it included all the logistics I would need in order to get there, not realising that sometimes "yes, that sounds great" is enough.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: It seemed to want to have the last word quite a bit, occasionally getting stuck in a loop of "okay" and "thank you's".
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: Meta is relying on people choosing to trust it with even more of their personal data, despite a rather dubious track record historically with its social networks and a growing backlash against AI in general.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: I asked Linda - my new dedicated if occasionally clunky assistant - if it wanted to take people's jobs.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "I'm here to take the admin and the fiddly bits off your plate," it replied, leaving me to do the "thinking".
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: "Everything you do is stuff I would usually think about," I responded.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: And Linda is helping fuel that revolution, one calendar invite at a time.
sentences.article_title: Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

sentences.text: While the movie's flying cars haven't - quite - materialised yet in the real world, Blade Runner's themes of technological progress and the threats it poses feel just as relevant.

sentences.text: At least that's what the cast and crew of Blade Runner 2099, a new TV series set in the same universe, are hoping.

sentences.text: BBC Newsbeat spoke to stars Hunter Schafer, Lewis Gribben and Dimitri Abold, plus showrunner Silka Luisa, to ask why they think themes of artificial consciousness and existential threats still resonate.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: The original Blade Runner, directed by Sir Ridley Scott, is considered a sci-fi classic that had a long-lasting influence on the genre.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: It told the story of Detective Deckard, played by Harrison Ford, who hunted down synthetic humans known as replicants.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: Schafer says her first exposure to the series was actually marketing for Blade Runner 2049 - the film sequel starring Ford and Ryan Gosling in 2017.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "I never thought I'd have the opportunity to make an addition to the world," she says.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "And so when that opportunity came along, I was quite thrilled." Blade Runner 2099 is set 80 years after the original film, and portrays a Los Angeles where replicants have taken over.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: Schafer plays Cora, a fugitive human forced to team up with replicant Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh), as she tries to track down an artefact that could save humanity.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: Schafer stars alongside Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh in the new TV adaptation The series lands at a time when there are disagreements about the nature of the threat AI could pose to humans .
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "I think it's particularly relevant right now, especially for the youth and young people who are inheriting a world that's asking a lot of the same questions that the show asks," says Schafer.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "I think that's timely and hopefully helpful to some degree." But Blade Runner 2099 isn't "necessarily about just AI", says showrunner Luisa.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "It's this bigger question of what is the world going to be in 15 years and how can you plan for it?" she says.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: The first Blade Runner also touched on themes of corporate greed and environmental damage, which are evident in the new series.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: Luisa hopes the theme of a future that "is not going to be what you were promised" resonates with viewers today.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "The idea that you were born into a world and you thought you were expecting certain aspects of your life just to roll out," she says.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "That system is collapsing.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: And so what will be your place in whatever comes next?" Blade Runner 2049 won awards and scored well with reviewers, but reports suggested it didn't hit box office targets.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: This was partly blamed on marketing for the film trying to appeal more to existing fans than new ones - so what would the cast say to get younger viewers on board?
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "It's just a very rich world," says Gribben, who plays Cora's younger brother Elias.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "It makes you want to learn more." Gribben also points out that Blade Runner 2099, which employed "hundreds of artists and craftspeople" according to its makers, is a celebration of traditional film-making despite its themes.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "I think a lot of people crave human stories," he says.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "They crave new kind of worlds and new things.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "And I think studios will rely more on technology to make better-looking movies, but they won't have that soul." Abold, who plays Cora's human ally Bebeto, says one of the show's key messages is about "the connections that you make".
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "And the connections that you make are the foundation of humanity," he says.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "Because at the end of the day, all we have is ourselves and each other, right?
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: There was praise for the lead performances, the show's visual style and the way it updates the themes established in previous series entries.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: The most common criticism was the show's pacing, with several critics describing it as a slow-burn and questioning whether Blade Runner worked as well off the big screen.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: Schafer says she felt a lot of pressure when she signed up for the show, "It's something that we were all aware of when making this show," she says.

sentences.text: "Everybody who was working on this show loves Blade Runner.
sentences.article_title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator

sentences.text: "Most people who love film-making love Blade Runner, everybody brought their best to work.

sentences.text: The museum's Our Time space will host events among 13 large installations and flocks of sheep benches Ten years ago the Museum of London announced it would be leaving its former home to move to the abandoned halls of Smithfield Market.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Now rebranded London Museum, it is set to open its doors to the public on Saturday after a £437m project.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: So what's it like inside?
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Leaning back on a leather sofa, museum director Sharon Ament looks across a vast brick-lined space that once bustled with market traders but is now filling with its newest visitors.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: "I really love this space, it just makes me smile every time I come in - it's actually joyful," she says.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: The vast room, now known as Our Time, is dotted with installations reflecting living memory.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: In one corner a life-size mechanical giraffe flicks its ears in front of a lit-up NHS sign representing lockdown.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Another wall has remnants of London's former greyhound tracks.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Near it is the old switchboard from Buckingham Palace.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: And beneath the magnificent domed ceiling roam several flocks of large plastic sheep which Ament encourages people to "pull up and take a seat" on.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: "There are grins on people's faces, so I think we've pulled something rather incredible off," she says.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Here, data-filled digital displays tell of London in the moment, beside a Banksy-graffitied sentry box and the last bell to be cast at the historic Whitechapel Bell Foundry .
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Next they enter the former General Market with its sheep, giraffe and signage.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: This is the space where events like late-night house parties and dinner clubs will be held beside shops and eateries, including former Victorian cocoa rooms that will be open 24 hours a day at weekends.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Such hints of the building's past are everywhere.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Halfway up the walls are the restored fireplaces of the traders' former offices, along with twisting metal staircases that once led up to them.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: "Whenever we've found historic fabric, we've restored it or kept it, and we want to show the layers of history," explains Alec Shaw, who has led the entire project.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Restoring a Victorian relic that was abandoned in the 1990s "really tested all of us", he admits, and that was before the logistics involved in designing a new museum from the venue's seven-million object collection.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Five thousand of these are now on site and another 300,000 are due to arrive for when the former Poultry Market becomes a museum space in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: "We think you could take at least eight hours to see every object downstairs, and that means you're going to keep coming back.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: "The best museums are those that you go, 'Right I'll do that one today.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: I'll do this gallery next time,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Our Past is based in the building's basement and tells a weaving story of London through five different chapters Queen Victoria's mourning dress is among the objects on display A wide staircase to one side descends into what is called Past Time.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Down here is what once was street level of Roman London, and curator Annette Day explains that "we felt that right in the guts, in the earth of the city, that was the place where we should explore London".
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: A weaving route beneath a seven-metre-high brick vaulted ceiling tells the capital's story.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: It starts with the city's creation by the Romans and moves through medieval times and London's place as the centre of the British Empire, before ending with the 2012 Olympic Games, a time when "London looked at itself and the world looked at London", says Day.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Along the way are all manner of objects.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: There's Charles I's execution vest, Queen Victoria's mourning dress, a white 1960s Ford Cortina, an overstuffed taxidermy cat called Oliver and the shimmering Elizabethan jewellery of the Cheapside Hoard.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Large illustrations are incorporated with historic objects to tell the story of the Great Fire of London Oliver the overstuffed taxidermy cat was once a Londoner's pet Galleries on either side also focus on specific moments.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: One features a recreated Roman room with amphoras - two-handled jars - a mosaic floor and the pieces of a magnificent wall painting found in Lime Street 20 years ago that hang on the wall.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Another uses large comic illustrations based on new research to tell the story of the Great Fire of London in an attempt to reflect the subject's inclusion in Key Stage 1 of the national curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: Further along still, two other archways branch off to look at the lives of Londoners and the city's landscape, placing objects from across the ages alongside each other.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: The delicately feathered Dying Swan outfit worn by lauded Russian dancer Anna Pavlova stands beside the stage outfit of Edwardian music hall star Kitty Lord in one case, while another shows 2,000 years of London-made shoes.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: One case is even filled with toilets and chamber pots from medieval times to today.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: And to carry on that subject, on the far wall a small porthole frames a chunk of the eponymous Whitechapel fatberg , not far from the huge glass window that looks out on passing Thameslink trains (whose passengers apparently are yet to notice they are now being watched).
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: She sees the museum as a shared space for everyone, somewhere for Londoners and tourists alike to connect with people and stories from the past and now.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: "Think of this as like one of my favourite buses, the number 63 bus.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: You meet the world on it.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: And you meet the world in here." Most important of all, she says, is that the London Museum must always represent and reflect the city it is in.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: "The story of London is tough and joyful at the same time.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: That's why we use 'grit and glitter' as a tagline - it's both of those things, those dualities can exist.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: And we shouldn't be frightened of that history," she says.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: "We are making a museum and it will never stop, just like London never stops.
sentences.article_title: Fatbergs, feathers and flocks of sheep - inside the new London Museum

sentences.text: There's always cranes in London and there'll always be new things in London Museum." sentences.text: Cameron Bancroft (left) was caught using sandpaper on the ball during Australia's third Test in South Africa in 2018 Cricket Australia (CA) will not like what it finds from a forum into the sandpaper scandal, according to former England captain Michael Vaughan.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: CA has invited evidence into the ball-tampering controversy of Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018 following weeks of speculation over which players and coaches were involved.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: "It's very clear to me that Cricket Australia are going to find some things out that they're probably not going to want to find out," Vaughan told the Test Match Special podcast.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: "If they don't release the truth of what they find in this forum out to the public, we're going to get back to square one." The row over the ball-tampering scandal was reignited by claims published in the autobiography of former Australia batter Usman Khawaja.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: At the time of the controversy, only batter Cameron Bancroft, then captain Steve Smith and his deputy David Warner were punished for the cheating plot.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: Khawaja alleged all players and coaches knew of the tampering and should have taken responsibility, a testimony supported by Bancroft, Warner and squad players Chadd Sayers and Jon Holland.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: Former coach Darren Lehmann and Australia captain Pat Cummins have been among those who have denied knowledge or involvement.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: Although McLeod will publish her findings and CA will give a public response, evidence will remain confidential, there will be no new attribution of responsibility and no further sanctions.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: The scope of the forum will extend to the Australian home season prior to the 2018 tour of South Africa, which included their 4-0 Ashes defeat of England.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: Writing in his autobiography in 2019, former England opener and captain Sir Alastair Cook said the tourists had suspicions about how Australia were getting the ball to move, and that Warner later admitted to using substances attached to the strapping on his hands in domestic matches.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: Cook's suspicions related to the third Test in Perth.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: Heavy overnight rain had delayed the fifth day at the Waca, when England were attempting to save the Test.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: When play finally began, the outfield was wet, conditions that would normally prevent any reverse swing.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan

sentences.text: Cook claimed that Australia found an "inordinate" amount of reverse.
sentences.article_title: Cricket Australia may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan
